rw: Writing 'Per my last email' in an angry tone sounds blaming and sarcastic. It can spark conflict and damage the working relationship, even when the writer was right.

ww.It improves teamwork by showing strong l: Sarcastic phrasing does not show leadership. It makes the coworker feel accused, which hurts cooperation and weakens teamwork instead of building it.
ww.It ensures the coworker will always resp: An angry reminder does not guarantee a faster response. Hostile messages usually make people defensive or less willing to help, so replies may even slow down.
ww.It makes the whole message sound more pr: Anger does not make writing more professional. Professional messages stay calm, specific and respectful, and this phrase read in anger comes across as passive aggressive.

rw: Clear, simple words help readers understand faster with fewer errors. That saves time, avoids misunderstandings and lets the reader act on the message.

ww.Complex words always impress customers w: Complex words do not always impress customers. They can confuse readers and hide the message, so clear words are usually more effective in business writing.
ww.Simple words are not allowed in formal r: Simple words are allowed in formal reports, and many reports prefer them. Plain language makes the writing accurate and easy for any reader to follow.
ww.Short words take much more time to write: Short words are not harder to write well. Plain, short wording usually takes less effort for the reader, and clear writing is a skill worth practicing.

rw: Reviewing for clarity, accuracy and errors after writing catches mistakes you missed while drafting. A careful revision makes the document stronger and more professional.

ww.Add extra words to make it a lot longer: Adding extra words makes a document longer without making it better. Editing usually cuts unneeded words so the main point is easier to find.
ww.Change the topic halfway through the who: Changing the topic halfway confuses readers and breaks the flow. Revising should keep the document focused on its purpose.
ww.Send it right away without reading it ag: Sending without rereading lets typos and mistakes through. Editing means reading the draft again and fixing problems before it goes out.

rw: Admitting you do not know and offering to follow up is honest and professional. It keeps trust and shows you care about giving a correct answer later.

ww.Make up an answer so you look well prepa: Making up an answer is dishonest and can mislead the audience. If the invented answer is wrong, you lose credibility.
ww.Ignore the question and move on to the n: Ignoring the question disrespects the listener. It makes you seem evasive and leaves the person without help.
ww.Tell the listener the question is not im: Telling the listener the question is unimportant is rude and dismissive. It discourages people from taking part and damages your credibility as a presenter.

rw: CRM means managing interactions and information to build lasting customer relationships. Software stores purchase history and contacts so staff can serve each customer better.

ww.A rule that requires customers to buy a: Requiring customers to buy every month is a contract or subscription term. CRM is about managing interactions and information, not forcing purchases.
ww.A method for lowering prices for all cus: Lowering prices for everyone is a pricing choice. CRM instead uses customer information to build relationships, not just to cut prices.
ww.A way to keep customers from sharing fee: CRM does not stop customers from sharing feedback. It usually collects feedback so a business can respond to what customers say.

rw: Listening first calms the customer and shows respect. Apologizing and asking what outcome would help then points the conversation toward a real solution.

ww.Say it is not the company's responsibili: Saying it is not the company's responsibility dismisses the complaint. It makes the customer angrier and damages trust.
ww.Ask the customer to call back again some: Asking the customer to call back shifts the work onto them. The problem stays unresolved and the customer feels ignored.
ww.Explain why the customer should have ord: Blaming the customer for ordering late is defensive and unfair. A late delivery is the company's problem to address.

rw: Businesses collect feedback to learn what customers want and to improve products and service. It shows strengths to keep and problems to fix.

ww.To reduce the number of customers served: Collecting feedback is not about serving fewer customers. Businesses want more satisfied customers, and feedback helps them get there.
ww.To avoid training employees and save mon: Feedback does not replace training. Employees still need training, and feedback can even show where more training is needed.
ww.To prove to customers that the company i: Feedback is not a way to prove the company is always right. It is a way to find out where the company can do better.

rw: A free item after ten purchases rewards repeat business and builds loyalty. Customers have a reason to keep returning, and the business benefits from steady sales.

ww.It guarantees every customer will be sat: A loyalty program cannot guarantee satisfaction for every customer. It rewards repeat purchases but does not replace good products and service.
ww.It discourages customers from returning: A free item after ten purchases encourages customers to come back. It does not discourage returns, which is the opposite of its aim.
ww.It reduces the quality of service given: A reward program does not lower service quality. It adds value for the customer and works best with good service.

rw: A customer service mindset means putting customers' needs at the center of your actions. It makes staff look for ways to help rather than just follow routine.

ww.Avoiding customers who ask many question: Avoiding customers who ask many questions is the opposite of a service mindset. Questions show what the customer needs.
ww.Focusing only on closing as many sales a: Focusing only on closing sales treats customers as targets. A service mindset values helping them, even when no sale follows.
ww.Following only the rules that benefit th: Following only rules that benefit the company ignores the customer. A service mindset balances policy with the customer's needs.

rw: Explaining the policy kindly and offering any allowed options respects the customer and the rules. It can offer store credit or an exchange to keep goodwill.

ww.Argue that the customer should have read: Arguing that the customer should have read the policy is confrontational. It may be true, but it loses goodwill and rarely settles things.
ww.Refuse and walk away without explaining: Refusing and walking away without explanation is rude and leaves the customer confused. They deserve to know why.
ww.Break the policy without telling a manag: Breaking policy without telling a manager is unfair to others and can cause problems. Exceptions should be approved by someone with authority.

rw: Greeting customers warmly and showing genuine interest in their needs builds rapport. Customers feel valued and are more likely to trust and return.

ww.Talk only about the company's profits an: Talking about company profits is about the business, not the customer. It does nothing to build a connection.
ww.Use technical terms that the customer ca: Using technical terms the customer cannot follow creates distance. Plain language makes people feel respected and understood.
ww.Avoid eye contact with them in order to: Avoiding eye contact comes across as cold or uninterested. Eye contact shows attention and helps build rapport.

rw: Helping each customer quickly while staying courteous delivers both parts of the promise, fast and friendly. It makes the brand promise real for customers.

ww.Taking long breaks during the busy perio: Taking long breaks during busy periods leaves customers waiting. It breaks the promise of fast service.
ww.Ignoring customers until they ask three: Ignoring customers until they ask several times is neither fast nor friendly. It contradicts the brand promise.
ww.Speaking sharply to customers who ask fo: Speaking sharply to customers is unfriendly. It breaks the promise of friendly service.

rw: A customer touch point is any interaction a customer has with a business. Examples are the website, store visits, calls and ads, and each shapes the customer's impression.

ww.A tax that a customer pays on top of the: A tax a customer pays is a cost. A touch point is any contact with the business.
ww.A coupon given only to employees of the: A coupon for employees is an internal perk. A touch point is about customers.
ww.A product that is out of stock in the st: An out-of-stock product is a supply problem. A touch point is an interaction.

rw: A confusing website but helpful staff shows the experience can vary across touch points. A business should work to make each one equally good.

ww.Employees should avoid helping customers: Employees helping customers is a good thing, as the store staff did. The feedback suggests no change to that.
ww.Stores should close their doors for good: Closing stores is an extreme reaction. The feedback praised the staff, so the stores are working well.
ww.Online service is not important to custo: Online service matters to customers. The confusing website shows it needs improvement, not that it is unimportant.

rw: Following up shows care and can reveal problems or new needs. It keeps the relationship going and can lead to repeat sales.

ww.It lets the business avoid honoring warr: Following up does not help avoid warranties. Honoring them is part of good service.
ww.It reduces the chance the customer retur: Following up makes it more likely the customer will return. It shows the business cares after the sale.
ww.It replaces the need for good products o: Following up does not replace good products or service. It supports them.

rw: A customer database or CRM system stores purchase history and preferences. Staff can use it to personalize service and marketing.

ww.A printer used for office documents: A printer is for printing documents. It cannot track purchase history or preferences.
ww.A calculator used in the back office: A calculator does arithmetic. It does not store customer information.
ww.A security camera in the parking lot: A security camera records video. It does not track purchases.

rw: When lattes sell out each morning, demand exceeds supply at $4. The shop can raise the price until supply and demand match.

ww.Price will not matter to buyers: Price matters to buyers when goods run short. A shortage at $4 means buyers want more than is supplied.
ww.Price will tend to fall to zero: Price does not fall to zero when lattes sell out. Strong demand and limited supply push the price up.
ww.Price will stay fixed by law: Prices in a market are not fixed by law here. The shop can raise the price when demand is strong.

rw: Opportunity cost is the value of the next best alternative you give up. Every choice has one because resources are limited.

ww.The profit earned from a sale of goods t: Profit from a sale is revenue minus costs. Opportunity cost is about alternatives given up.
ww.The tax added to a purchase made at a st: A tax on a purchase is a tax. Opportunity cost is not a payment.
ww.The price you pay for a product at check: The price you pay at checkout is a money cost. Opportunity cost includes what else you could have done.

rw: The law of demand says that when price rises, quantity demanded falls. Fewer people take long trips when gas gets expensive.

ww.Comparative advantage: Comparative advantage explains trade between countries. It does not explain fewer road trips when gas rises.
ww.The law of supply: The law of supply says suppliers offer more at higher prices. The example is about buyers cutting back.
ww.Diminishing returns: Diminishing returns concerns production. The example describes consumer behavior.

rw: A haircut is a service, an activity performed for someone. You cannot hold or store it.

ww.Some shoes: Shoes are a physical good. You can touch and own them.
ww.A bicycle: A bicycle is a physical good. It is made and sold as a product.
ww.Bottled water: Bottled water is a physical good. A service is an activity, not an item.

rw: When unemployment rises, fewer people earn wages. Consumer spending probably falls because incomes drop and people feel less secure.

ww.It will not change at all: Spending usually changes when many people lose jobs. A rise from 4% to 9% unemployment cuts incomes.
ww.It will likely rise: Spending would not rise when more people are out of work. They have less income to spend.
ww.It will become illegal: Spending does not become illegal. It simply falls when fewer people are earning.

rw: Competition is rivalry among businesses that sell similar products. It pushes firms to improve quality and keep prices fair.

ww.A government rule that sets all prices o: A government rule that sets prices is price control. Competition is rivalry among businesses.
ww.An agreement among businesses to share p: Agreeing to share profits is collusion. It reduces real competition and is often illegal.
ww.A single business with no rivals in its: A single business with no rivals is a monopoly. Competition needs several firms.

rw: Specializing lets a business become more efficient and productive. Focusing on one product builds skill and lowers costs.

ww.It will no longer need any customers at: A business always needs customers. Specializing does not remove that.
ww.It avoids all competition from other fir: Specializing does not avoid competition. Other firms may sell the same product.
ww.It must always produce less than other f: Specializing does not force less output. It usually raises output per worker.

rw: When the central bank raises rates, borrowing becomes more expensive and may decline. Firms often delay investments.

ww.Borrowing becomes free for all small bus: Higher rates do not make borrowing free. They raise the cost of loans.
ww.Borrowing increases because loans cost l: Loans cost more, not less, when rates rise. Borrowing tends to fall.
ww.Borrowing is banned for all businesses b: Raising rates does not ban borrowing. It only makes it costlier.

rw: Capital includes tools, machinery and buildings used to make goods. It is a factory's physical equipment.

ww.Land: Land means natural resources, such as soil and minerals. It is not tools and machinery.
ww.Enterprise: Enterprise is the entrepreneur's initiative and risk taking. It is not the tools themselves.
ww.Labor: Labor is human work. Machinery is capital.

rw: A tariff raises the price of imported steel. Domestic buyers may pay more for steel, either imported or home-made.

ww.They will receive steel for free: Tariffs do not make steel free. They add a tax that raises prices.
ww.They see imported steel get cheaper: A tariff makes imports more expensive, not cheaper. Buyers see higher prices.
ww.They will no longer need any steel: Steel is still needed. A tariff changes its price, not whether buyers want it.

rw: A market economy relies on consumer demand and the choices of businesses. Firms produce what customers will pay for.

ww.Traditions passed down for many generati: Traditions guide a traditional economy. A market economy relies on demand and business choices.
ww.Random selection of products in the stor: Random selection is not how markets decide. Demand and profit guide choices.
ww.Decisions made only by a central planner: A central planner decides in a command economy. In a market economy, many people decide.

rw: Globalization is the growing connection of economies through trade and investment. Goods, money and ideas cross borders more freely.

ww.A steady decline in international trade: Globalization is not a decline in trade. It is a growing connection among nations.
ww.A tax on all exports sent out of the cou: A tax on exports is a trade policy. It is not globalization.
ww.A rule limiting each country to local go: A rule limiting countries to local goods is protectionism. It is the opposite of globalization.

rw: Doubling workers in the same small kitchen raises output only a little. That shows the law of diminishing returns, where each added worker adds less.

ww.Comparative advantage in trade: Comparative advantage is about trade between countries. It does not explain a crowded kitchen.
ww.Economies of scale in a firm: Economies of scale means costs fall as output grows. Here output barely rises, so it does not apply.
ww.Price discrimination by firms: Price discrimination is charging different prices to different buyers. It has nothing to do with workers.

rw: Taxes fund government services such as roads, schools and safety. They pay for goods the market may not supply well.

ww.They replace the need for money in the w: Taxes do not replace money. They collect it from people and firms.
ww.They prevent all business from making a: Taxes do not prevent profit. Businesses still earn profits after taxes.
ww.They set the price of every product in t: Taxes do not set prices. Markets and firms set most prices.

rw: A business cycle is repeating periods of economic expansion and contraction. The economy grows, peaks, shrinks and recovers.

ww.A rule about the hours of business for a: A rule about store hours is a regulation. A business cycle is an economic pattern.
ww.A single period of constant growth with: Constant growth with no decline is not a cycle. A cycle repeats ups and downs.
ww.A fixed schedule for opening new stores: A schedule for opening stores is a company plan. It is not an economic cycle.

rw: Empathy is understanding and sharing the feelings of others. It improves teamwork and trust.

ww.Ignoring a coworker's problems to stay o: Ignoring coworkers' problems is the opposite of empathy. It shows no care for their feelings.
ww.Avoiding any emotional conversation with: Avoiding emotional conversation is not empathy. Empathy means engaging with feelings.
ww.Agreeing with everything that others say: Agreeing with everything is not empathy. You can understand without agreeing.

rw: Staying calm and asking for specific feedback shows self-control. You manage emotions and learn from the comment.

ww.Leave the room and refuse to return: Leaving the room and refusing to return avoids the issue. It shows poor self-control.
ww.Say the coworker is not qualified to com: Saying the coworker is not qualified attacks the person. It shows poor self-control.
ww.Raise your voice and defend yourself: Raising your voice and defending yourself shows poor control. It escalates the situation.

rw: Honesty about a mistake builds trust and lets problems be fixed quickly. Others can help once they know.

ww.It lets you avoid taking responsibility: Honesty does not avoid responsibility. It means taking it.
ww.It makes mistakes unimportant to the res: Honesty does not make mistakes unimportant. It helps handle them.
ww.It guarantees you will never be correcte: Honesty does not guarantee you will never be corrected. Everyone makes mistakes.

rw: Accepting feedback for growth means using others' comments to improve your skills. It helps you become better at your job.

ww.Reject all comments that are critical of: Rejecting all critical comments blocks growth. You miss chances to improve.
ww.Argue until others change their opinion: Arguing until others change their opinion avoids learning. It wastes time.
ww.Ask for feedback and then never act on i: Asking for feedback and never acting on it wastes it. Growth needs action.

rw: Keeping personal information confidential respects a coworker's privacy. It builds trust.

ww.Post personal details on social media: Posting personal details on social media breaks privacy. It exposes a coworker.
ww.Read a coworker's personal messages: Reading someone's personal messages invades privacy. It breaks trust.
ww.Share a coworker's health news widely: Sharing a coworker's health news widely breaks confidentiality. It could harm them.

rw: Listening to both sides and guiding them to a shared solution is fair. It helps them work together.

ww.Tell them both to stop talking about it: Telling both to stop talking about it leaves the disagreement unresolved. It may grow.
ww.Choose a side right away without hearing: Choosing a side without hearing both is unfair. It would breed resentment.
ww.Remove both people from the project perm: Removing both people permanently is extreme. It does not solve the disagreement.

rw: A stereotype is a fixed, oversimplified belief about a group of people. It ignores individual differences and can lead to unfair treatment.

ww.A compliment given to a coworker for goo: A compliment is praise for a person. A stereotype is a belief about a group.
ww.A rule that a company must follow under: A legal rule is a regulation. A stereotype is a belief.
ww.A fact proven through research about eve: A stereotype is not a proven fact about every person in a group. It is a generalization.

rw: Considering cultural differences before drawing conclusions is fair. In some cultures, avoiding eye contact shows respect.

ww.End the interview immediately and send t: Ending the interview over eye contact is unfair. Norms vary across cultures.
ww.Assume the candidate is dishonest and re: Assuming the candidate is dishonest is a stereotype. It ignores culture.
ww.Tell the candidate to change culture bef: Telling a candidate to change culture is disrespectful. Interviewers should adapt.

rw: Approaching challenges with a willingness to solve them shows a positive attitude. It helps the whole team.

ww.Giving up when a problem appears at the: Giving up when a problem appears shows a negative attitude. A positive attitude keeps trying.
ww.Complaining about every new task the man: Complaining about every new task shows a negative attitude. It spreads negativity.
ww.Refusing to help others with their work: Refusing to help others shows a negative attitude. A positive one supports coworkers.

rw: Recognizing others' contributions builds morale. People feel valued and work harder.

ww.The team did not do any real work on the: Crediting the whole team does not mean they did no work. It acknowledges their effort.
ww.The leader has no role in the project at: The leader still has a role. Sharing credit shows modesty and does not erase that role.
ww.Recognition lowers motivation in the tea: Recognition raises motivation. It does not lower it.

rw: A code of ethics is a set of principles for honest and responsible behavior. It guides decisions and protects the business's reputation.

ww.A schedule for employee breaks and lunch: A schedule for breaks is an HR policy. A code of ethics sets principles.
ww.A plan for the next product launch by th: A plan for a product launch is a marketing plan. It is not about ethics.
ww.A list of the lowest-priced products tha: A list of low-priced products is a price list. It is not a code of ethics.

rw: Reporting it and helping correct it is honest. It protects the customer and the firm's reputation.

ww.Blame the customer for this: Blaming the customer is dishonest and unfair. The firm made the error.
ww.Wait until someone else notices: Waiting for someone else to notice avoids responsibility. The employee knows now.
ww.Keep quiet as the company gains: Keeping quiet because the company gains is dishonest. It takes advantage of the customer.

rw: Willingness to take calculated risks is common among successful entrepreneurs. They accept uncertainty after weighing the odds.

ww.Refusing to adapt to any kind of change: Refusing to adapt to change hurts a business. Successful entrepreneurs adapt.
ww.Avoiding all decisions made at work: Avoiding decisions stalls a business. Entrepreneurs decide.
ww.Waiting for others to start the tasks: Waiting for others to start tasks lacks initiative. Entrepreneurs take the lead.

rw: Selling handmade bracelets shows identifying a need or opportunity and acting on it. That is the core of entrepreneurship.

ww.Avoiding any customer interaction with t: Selling bracelets online involves customers. It is not avoiding interaction.
ww.Relying only on government funds to run: A student selling bracelets is not relying on government funds. It is a small self-funded venture.
ww.Closing a business after the very first: Closing after one sale does not match the example. The student keeps selling.

rw: A business plan is a document describing goals, strategies and finances. It guides the business and helps win funding.

ww.A license to operate in any state of the: A license to operate is permission. A business plan describes goals and strategy.
ww.A list of competitors' phone numbers and: A list of competitor contacts is research. It is not a plan.
ww.A receipt for every sale made at the sto: A receipt records a sale. A business plan looks ahead.

rw: New businesses seek loans or investors to pay start-up costs such as equipment and inventory. They often lack enough cash at the start.

ww.To avoid having customers come into the: Businesses want customers. A loan does not help avoid them.
ww.To prevent paying taxes on any money the: Loans do not avoid taxes. Taxes still apply.
ww.To keep the business a secret from rival: Loans are not for secrecy. Businesses must share plans with lenders.

rw: Hiring neighbors and buying from local farms shows the impact of small business on the local economy. It creates jobs and income locally.

ww.A government-run enterprise that is owne: A restaurant hiring neighbors and buying from local farms is a private business. It is not state-run.
ww.A tax-free business structure that has n: A tax-free structure with no owners does not exist. The restaurant has an owner.
ww.A decline in local jobs as small firms c: Hiring neighbors adds local jobs. It is not a decline.

rw: A sole proprietorship is a business owned and run by one person. It is simple to start, but the owner has unlimited liability.

ww.A business owned by the government: A business owned by the government is a public enterprise. A sole proprietorship is private.
ww.A business owned by many shareholders: A business owned by many shareholders is a corporation. A sole proprietorship has one owner.
ww.A business owned by two or more partners: A business owned by two or more partners is a partnership. A sole proprietorship has one owner.

rw: Support and a recognized brand from the franchisor are advantages of a franchise. Training and marketing help new owners succeed.

ww.Guaranteed profit with no risk to the ow: No business is risk free. A franchise does not guarantee profit.
ww.Freedom to change the products without a: Franchisees usually need approval to change products. The brand must stay consistent.
ww.No fees ever paid to the franchisor or h: Franchisees pay fees and royalties to the franchisor. They are not free.

rw: Researching whether enough demand exists is the sensible first step. It tests the idea before spending money.

ww.Open immediately without any research: Opening immediately without research is risky. It could waste money.
ww.Ignore the customers and their requests: Ignoring customers' requests wastes an opportunity. They are showing demand.
ww.Wait for a competitor to start it first: Waiting for a competitor to start gives away the lead. It lets someone else win.

rw: Innovation means creating new or improved products, services or methods. It helps a business stand out and grow.

ww.Raising prices without adding any value: Raising prices without adding value is not innovation. It gives buyers nothing new.
ww.Copying a competitor exactly with no cha: Copying a competitor exactly is imitation. Innovation adds something new.
ww.Keeping the same product forever and nev: Keeping the same product forever is the opposite of innovation. It ignores change.

rw: Honest practices build trust with customers and partners. Trust leads to repeat sales and strong relationships.

ww.Ethics reduce the need for customers in: Ethics do not reduce the need for customers. They help win them.
ww.Ethics only matter for large firms, not: Ethics matter for all firms, large and small. A small shop depends on reputation.
ww.Ethics are optional for owners of a smal: Ethics are not optional for small businesses. Customers expect honest dealing.

rw: International trade gives small businesses access to a larger customer base. It opens many more potential buyers.

ww.Removal of all competition there: Removing all competition abroad is not an opportunity. Foreign markets have competitors too.
ww.Guaranteed lower costs abroad: Lower costs abroad are not guaranteed. Shipping and rules can add costs.
ww.Automatic exemption from laws: No firm is automatically exempt from laws. It must follow local rules.

rw: A budget is a plan for how income will be spent and saved. It helps a person or business control money.

ww.A list of tax rates set by the state for: Tax rates are set by governments. A budget is a spending plan.
ww.A bank loan application form from the lo: A loan application is a request to a bank. It is not a plan for money.
ww.A record of past purchases with no plan: A record of past purchases is a history. A budget plans ahead.

rw: The balance sheet shows a business's financial position at a point in time. It lists assets, liabilities and equity.

ww.The income statement: The income statement shows results over a period. It does not show position at a point in time.
ww.The sales invoice: A sales invoice is a bill for a sale. It does not show financial position.
ww.The paycheck stub: A paycheck stub shows an employee's pay. It does not show a firm's position.

rw: Owner's equity equals assets minus liabilities. $80,000 minus $50,000 is $30,000.

ww.$50,000: $50,000 is the liabilities. Equity is assets minus liabilities.
ww.$130,000: $130,000 adds assets and liabilities. Equity subtracts liabilities from assets.
ww.$80,000: $80,000 is the assets. Equity is what is left after liabilities.

rw: An income statement reports revenue, expenses and profit or loss for a period. It shows how a business performed.

ww.The assets a business owns on one given: The assets on one date appear on the balance sheet. The income statement covers a period.
ww.The list of employees and their pay rate: A staff list and pay rates are HR records. They are not on an income statement.
ww.The cash balance in a personal checking: A personal checking balance is not a business report. It does not show company results.

rw: The time value of money means money today is worth more than the same amount later. Money today can be invested to earn interest.

ww.Money loses all of its value over a sing: Money does not lose all value over a weekend. The idea is about time and interest.
ww.Money never changes in value over any le: Money changes in value over time. Inflation and interest affect it.
ww.Money is worth more the longer you wait: Waiting without investing does not add value. Waiting loses potential earnings.

rw: Profit equals revenue minus expenses. $200,000 less $150,000 is $50,000.

ww.$200,000: $200,000 is the revenue. Profit is revenue minus expenses.
ww.$350,000: $350,000 adds revenue and expenses together. Profit subtracts expenses.
ww.$150,000: $150,000 is the expenses. Profit is what remains after them.

rw: Stolen information can be used to open accounts or commit fraud. Protecting it prevents financial harm and legal trouble.

ww.It prevents all sales taxes on any of th: Identity theft protection has nothing to do with sales taxes. It protects personal information.
ww.It is only a concern for businesses, not: Identity theft affects individuals. It is not only a business worry.
ww.It improves your credit score each month: Protection does not improve your credit score by paying a fee. It prevents misuse of your information.

rw: Interest on a loan is the cost of borrowing money. The borrower pays it to the lender for use of the funds.

ww.The fee to open an account: The fee to open an account is an account charge. Interest is the cost of borrowing.
ww.A tax on your income earned: A tax on income is a tax. Interest is a lender's charge.
ww.The profit a borrower earns: The profit a borrower earns is not interest. The borrower pays interest to the lender.

rw: A cash flow statement shows whether the business can pay bills on time. It tracks cash coming in and going out.

ww.It lists every customer's name and addre: A customer list is a sales record. It is not a cash flow statement.
ww.It replaces the need for a budget, as it: A cash flow statement does not replace a budget. A budget plans ahead.
ww.It shows the company's trademarks and br: Trademarks are intangible assets. They do not appear on a cash flow statement.

rw: Diversification means spreading money across different investments. It lowers risk because one loss does not wipe out everything.

ww.Selling every investment at once for cas: Selling every investment at once is liquidation. It is not diversification.
ww.Putting all of your money in one single: Putting all your money in one stock is the opposite. It concentrates risk.
ww.Keeping all of your money at home in a d: Keeping money at home in a drawer is not investing. It earns nothing and could be stolen.

rw: Lenders use a credit score to judge how likely someone is to repay debt. It affects loan approval and interest rates.

ww.It measures a person's savings only, not: A credit score includes debts and payment history. It does not measure savings only.
ww.It decides a person's salary at their ma: A credit score does not decide salary. Employers set pay.
ww.It sets the price of groceries in all of: A credit score does not set grocery prices. Stores set them.

rw: Paying only the minimum lets interest build, and the debt takes much longer to repay. The total cost rises.

ww.No interest is charged on the unpaid bal: Interest is charged on the unpaid balance. Paying only the minimum leaves a large balance.
ww.The balance disappears quickly without a: The balance does not disappear with minimum payments. It shrinks very slowly.
ww.The credit limit rises, so less interest: The credit limit does not rise because of minimum payments. Interest still grows.

rw: Monthly rent is the same amount every month. It is a fixed expense.

ww.Snack money: Snack money varies each week. It is a variable expense.
ww.Movie tickets: Movie tickets are optional and vary. They are variable.
ww.Gift money: Gift money changes by occasion. It is variable.

rw: Reconciling a bank statement compares your records with the bank's to find differences. It catches errors, missing entries or fraud.

ww.Close the bank account and take out all: Reconciling does not close an account. It checks the records.
ww.Increase the credit limit so the owner c: It does not raise a credit limit. It is a checking process.
ww.Withdraw all money from the account to s: It does not withdraw all money. It compares figures.

rw: In orientation, new hires learn about the company, policies and their roles. It helps them settle in quickly.

ww.Employees are told to find answers on th: Orientation does not leave employees alone. New hires get guidance.
ww.Employees begin their retirement benefit: Retirement benefits do not start on the first day. Orientation introduces benefits.
ww.Employees are fired if they ask question: Employees are not fired for asking questions. Orientation encourages them.

rw: Training, fair pay and chances to advance make employees want to stay. They reduce turnover.

ww.Making schedules unpredictable for all t: Unpredictable schedules frustrate workers. They raise turnover.
ww.Cutting all training to save money and p: Cutting training and paying low wages pushes people to leave. It raises turnover.
ww.Ignoring employee suggestions for how to: Ignoring suggestions makes employees feel unheard. It can raise turnover.

rw: Treating all applicants fairly without discrimination follows employment law. It helps hire the best people.

ww.Ask about each candidate's family plans: Asking about family plans can lead to discrimination. It is unlawful in many places.
ww.Prefer candidates who look just like the: Preferring candidates who look like the manager is discrimination. It is unfair and illegal.
ww.Hire only the friends of all current emp: Hiring only friends of employees is unfair. It excludes qualified candidates.

rw: Investigating and correcting the situation under company policy is the right step. It protects employees and the firm.

ww.Ignore it to avoid conflict and keep eve: Ignoring age discrimination lets it continue. HR must act.
ww.Tell the employees to resign from their: Telling the employees to resign punishes the victims. It does not fix the problem.
ww.Wait for a lawsuit before acting on the: Waiting for a lawsuit lets harm continue. HR should act first.

rw: Training helps workers gain skills that improve performance. It makes them more productive and confident.

ww.It stops any employee from ever leaving: Training does not stop anyone from leaving. It may help keep staff.
ww.It removes the need for supervisors at w: Training does not remove the need for supervisors. Supervisors still guide work.
ww.It lowers all employee pay in the whole: Training does not lower pay. It can lead to raises.

rw: Companies keep employee records confidential to protect personal information and privacy. Leaks could cause harm.

ww.To hide the records from the employees: Records are not hidden from the employees themselves. They are kept private from others.
ww.To avoid paying employees for the work t: Confidentiality has nothing to do with avoiding pay. It protects privacy.
ww.To make hiring harder for the whole comp: Confidentiality does not make hiring harder. It protects workers.

rw: Software that tracks applicants and schedules interviews supports recruiting and selection. It helps manage hiring.

ww.Product pricing and sales: Product pricing and sales is a different function. Applicant tracking is for hiring.
ww.Tax filing for the year: Tax filing is an accounting job. It is not what applicant software does.
ww.Shipping and delivery: Shipping and delivery is operations. It does not involve applicants.

rw: Compensation is pay and benefits given to employees for their work. It includes wages, bonuses and insurance.

ww.The cost of company equipment and tools: Equipment cost is an expense. Compensation is what employees receive.
ww.A fine paid for breaking a rule at work: A fine is a penalty. Compensation rewards work.
ww.The price a customer pays for a product: The price a customer pays is revenue. Compensation is pay to staff.

rw: Recognizing employees means showing appreciation, such as praise or rewards. It boosts morale and motivation.

ww.Ignore results so everyone is treated eq: Ignoring results does not recognize anyone. Recognition rewards good work.
ww.Give rewards without any clear criteria: Rewards without criteria are unfair. Recognition should be based on clear standards.
ww.Criticize only mistakes and never praise: Criticizing mistakes only discourages staff. Recognition praises success.

rw: Data is raw facts and figures collected for use. Once analyzed, it becomes information.

ww.A finished report with conclusions: A finished report with conclusions is information. Data is raw.
ww.A person's opinion only, with no facts: An opinion with no facts is not data. Data is based on facts.
ww.A rule for company behavior at work: A rule for behavior is a policy. It is not data.

rw: Businesses back up files so they can recover information if data is lost or damaged. It prevents costly loss.

ww.To delete old files permanently from the: Backups do not delete old files. They make copies.
ww.To make files harder for employees to fi: Backups do not hide files. They keep copies safe.
ww.To increase the size of every file in th: Backups do not enlarge files. They duplicate them.

rw: Checking the source and accuracy before using a statistic prevents spreading false information. A statistic without a source may be wrong.

ww.Use it at once as it looks real: Using it at once because it looks real is risky. Looks can fool.
ww.Share it with customers as is: Sharing it with customers as is could spread false claims. It harms credibility.
ww.Ignore all other data sources: Ignoring all other sources is unwise. Good decisions use reliable data.

rw: A spreadsheet is used to organize and calculate numbers. It handles budgets, sales and totals.

ww.Editing photos and designing posters: Editing photos and posters needs design software. A spreadsheet works with data.
ww.Cooking recipes for a family meal: Cooking recipes belong in a kitchen. A spreadsheet is a business tool.
ww.Sending packages by mail or courier: Sending packages is a delivery task. A spreadsheet is not for mailing.

rw: Stocking more umbrellas when rain is forecast uses the pattern. It meets demand and avoids stockouts.

ww.Lower prices when it is sunny only each: Lowering prices when sunny does not use the pattern. The pattern is about rainy days.
ww.Stop selling umbrellas in the whole stor: Stopping umbrella sales ignores the data. Umbrellas sell on rainy days.
ww.Remove all weather information from plan: Removing weather information ignores a useful signal. Planning should use it.

rw: Protecting privacy and using data with permission is the key ethical issue. Customers should control their information.

ww.Collecting as much data as possible from: Collecting as much data as possible raises privacy risks. Only needed data should be collected.
ww.Hiding that data is collected from the u: Hiding that data is collected is dishonest. Users should be told.
ww.Selling the data to anyone who asks for: Selling data to anyone breaks trust and may be illegal. Data should be protected.

rw: An information system collects, stores and provides information for decisions. Managers rely on it to act on facts.

ww.To avoid keeping records of any kind for: Avoiding records is not the purpose. Information systems keep records.
ww.To replace all employees with machines t: An information system does not replace all employees. It supports them.
ww.To entertain customers while they wait i: Entertaining customers is not its purpose. It manages information.

rw: Data mining means searching large data sets for patterns and insights. Businesses use it to spot trends and customer habits.

ww.Writing code for websites and apps used: Writing code is programming. Data mining analyzes data.
ww.Deleting old files to free up space on t: Deleting old files is housekeeping. Data mining finds patterns.
ww.Digging for minerals underground with dr: Digging for minerals is mining in the literal sense. Data mining is digital.

rw: Audio fans who value sound quality and will pay more match high-end headphones. They are the likely target market.

ww.Businesses that do not use audio in thei: Businesses that do not use audio will not buy headphones. They are not a match.
ww.Shoppers who want only the cheapest opti: Shoppers who want only the cheapest option will not buy high-end products. They are the wrong target.
ww.People who never listen to music of any: People who never listen to music will not buy headphones. They are not a target.

rw: Needs, income, culture and personal preferences influence customer buying behavior. They shape what and when people buy.

ww.Only the weather on the day of the visit: Weather can matter, but it is not the only factor. Many influences exist.
ww.Only the name of the cashier at the fron: The cashier's name does not drive buying behavior. It is a trivial detail.
ww.Only the color of the store sign out fro: The sign color is a small factor. Many other things matter more.

rw: Improving the mobile app experience and offers fits younger customers who buy through mobile. It meets them where they shop.

ww.Raising prices for everyone who buys the: Raising prices does not respond to the habit. It could push buyers away.
ww.Stopping all research into what customer: Stopping research ignores what customers do. The company should keep learning.
ww.Removing all digital promotion for newsp: Removing digital promotion ignores the mobile habit. Young customers are online.

rw: Market research gathers information about customers and competitors. It helps a business make informed decisions.

ww.To avoid learning about customers or abo: Market research is not meant to avoid learning. It aims to learn.
ww.To set employee schedules for the next w: Setting schedules is an HR task. It is not research.
ww.To pay taxes owed to the state by the fi: Paying taxes is a legal duty. It is not research.

rw: Offering samples in a few stores and collecting feedback tests the snack on a small scale. It reveals problems before a national launch.

ww.Ask only the owner's family and a few fr: Asking only family and friends gives biased feedback. They may not be honest.
ww.Skip testing to save time and launch the: Skipping testing risks a costly failure. Testing saves money.
ww.Launch everywhere without feedback to re: Launching everywhere without feedback is risky. Problems would appear everywhere.

rw: Positioning means creating a distinct place for a product in customers' minds. It sets the product apart from rivals.

ww.Hiding the brand from the public in orde: Hiding the brand is the opposite of positioning. Positioning builds a brand image.
ww.Raising the price of every product that: Raising prices is a pricing decision. It is not positioning.
ww.Placing a product on the lowest shelf wh: Placing a product on a low shelf is merchandising. It is not positioning.

rw: Quality control helps ensure products meet standards. It reduces defects and complaints.

ww.It eliminates the need for customers: Quality control does not remove the need for customers. It satisfies them.
ww.It makes products cost more for no reaso: Quality control does not raise costs for no reason. It prevents bigger losses.
ww.It slows all delivery down to zero: It does not slow all delivery to zero. It checks products.

rw: Investigating the cause and fixing the process addresses the root problem. It stops defects from rising.

ww.Stop measuring defects in the factory: Stopping measurement hides the problem. It makes things worse.
ww.Ignore the defects until customers compl: Ignoring defects until customers complain damages reputation. Act early.
ww.Blame the workers without checking first: Blaming workers without checking is unfair. The cause may be in the process.

rw: A safety training program prevents accidents and injuries at work. It teaches safe methods and awareness.

ww.To increase sales and the firm's profits: Safety training is not meant to raise sales. Its goal is protection.
ww.To avoid keeping records of any accident: Avoiding records of accidents is wrong. Records help improve safety.
ww.To reduce the number of employees paid: It does not cut employees. It protects them.

rw: The supply chain is the network that moves a product from supplier to customer. It includes sourcing, making, storing and delivering.

ww.A list of company policies for the staff: A list of company policies is a handbook. The supply chain moves products.
ww.A chain of stores with the same name in: A chain of stores is a retail group. The supply chain is a network.
ww.The company's bank accounts and the cash: Bank accounts are finances. The supply chain is not about cash.

rw: Using more than one reliable supplier spreads risk. If one is delayed, another can deliver.

ww.Rely on one supplier with no backup: Relying on one supplier with no backup leaves the factory exposed. It repeats the risk.
ww.Buy parts only on the last day needed: Buying parts on the last day needed leaves no buffer. A delay would stop production.
ww.Stop tracking all inventory levels: Stopping tracking of inventory removes visibility. It makes shortages likelier.

rw: Project management is planning and controlling work to meet goals on time and in budget. It uses schedules, resources and monitoring.

ww.Setting prices for products sold by a fi: Setting prices is pricing. Project management organizes work.
ww.Selling products to customers in a store: Selling products is sales. It is not managing projects.
ww.Writing a company's mission statement fo: Writing a mission statement is a single task. It is not project management.

rw: Following security procedures protects company information and property. Everyone must follow the rules.

ww.Ignore visitors' badges when they come i: Ignoring visitor badges weakens security. Procedures require checking them.
ww.Leave doors unlocked to save time, so st: Leaving doors unlocked puts property at risk. Procedures require locking.
ww.Share passwords with coworkers to be hel: Sharing passwords breaks security rules. It risks company data.

rw: Organizing tasks by urgency and importance is prioritizing work. It ensures the most critical tasks come first.

ww.Product pricing: Product pricing is setting prices. Ordering tasks is prioritizing.
ww.Customer segmentation: Customer segmentation groups customers. It does not order tasks.
ww.Ad design work: Ad design is creative work. It is not task ordering.

rw: Overhead is ongoing costs not tied to one product, such as rent and utilities. It must be paid however much is made.

ww.The profit left after taxes are paid by: Profit after taxes is net income. Overhead is an ongoing cost.
ww.The price customers pay for goods in a s: The price customers pay is revenue. Overhead is a cost.
ww.The cost of materials for one item, whic: The cost of materials for one item is a direct or variable cost. Overhead is not tied to one product.
